notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Dawson Mercer takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4.

Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. Henry Thrun has taken his spot beside Mario Ferraro. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:14 together, up from 51% with DeMelo.

Isak Rosén is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. Viggo Björck has taken his spot beside Adam Lowry and Alex Iafallo. That line has had 81% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:18 together, up from 49% with Rosén.
Henry Thrun was added to the roster on Nov 14 and has played beside Mario Ferraro.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 11th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is day to day and has missed the last 18 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Michael Carcone is on injured reserve (upper-body surgery) and has missed the last 3 games.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-six forward. Vincent Trocheck has taken his spot beside Lawson Crouse and Clayton Keller.
Gregor Biber was added to the roster on Nov 22.

stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for sixth in the Central with 31 points, a point behind the Jets, tied for third. A regulation win for the Mammoth would lift them past the Jets.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a lot going for them
UTA.body: Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Jets’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

WPG.head: The Jets have a hill to climb
WPG.body: Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Jets’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Tilted ice, toward the Jets’ net
paras: The Jets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Winnipeg on Nov 23. The Mammoth have won two in a row, and the Jets have won three straight. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Jets fifth (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Mammoth seventh (tied for 14th). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Jets’ record (.593) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.524), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.574) says: their chances are worth about .705, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Jets get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd) and keep things calm after the whistle (4th lowest). They also create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd), and that sets up a fight with the Mammoth’s power play (9th), which could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (28th). The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Mammoth shoot a lot, but the Jets don’t.

Kyle Connor (22 G / 16 A / 38 P in 27 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (9 G / 25 A / 34 P in 27 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Utah. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (6 G / 25 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring. Logan Cooley (13 G / 16 A / 29 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, with seven points in his last five games.

Stuart Skinner (9-5-4 / .892 SV% in 19 GS) will likely start for Winnipeg. Utah has two options in net: Karel Vejmelka (8-7-2 / .864 SV% in 17 GS) and Sebastian Cossa (6-3-1 / .881 SV% in 10 GS). Vejmelka has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
